Subject: Private GPU pool — scaling trajectories, admission heuristics, and north-south shaping

Folks,

Summary: I ran a quick set of headroom projections for the ACME private deployment and want to align on two risk areas before we hand off a formal scope to NetGrid: (1) admission heuristics during sustained bimodal bursts, and (2) north-south (egress) shaping when model KV-cache warmup causes large spikes.

Key numbers (very rough):
- Target sustained throughput: 1200 tok/s per tenant peak window (90th pct)
- Typical burst shape: 10x short spikes (30–90s), 2–4x sustained ramps (10–30m)
- Budgeted capacity: 4000 tok/s per GPU pod (mixed gpus in cluster), target 6 pods for first cut

Open asks to NetGrid: can they offer headroom guarantees per pod (soft reservation + 2x burst cushion) and do they support programmable egress shaping at the top-of-rack? Laura — procurement/contract constraints we should signal now. Jonas — can you run the admission heuristic that trades off queue depth vs tail latency with these numbers?

Attachment: privgpu-scaling-scenarios-v2.xlsx (workbook with demand curves)

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, netgrid-eng@cloudco.com
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool — scaling trajectories, admission heuristics, and north-south shaping

Diego —

Quick pass on the numbers. I modeled three admission strategies against your burst shapes in the workbook: fixed-slot, proportional-queue, and probed-admit. High level:

- Fixed-slot (simple allocator): predictable latency for steady-state but will drop >30% of 10x spikes unless we overprovision heavily.
- Proportional-queue (queue-depth backpressure): smooths short spikes but increases 95th/99th latency by ~20–40ms for mid-sized requests. Better when KV-cache warmup is amortized.
- Probed-admit (fast probe tokens + ramp): best for mixed tail — accepts more of the spike while keeping 99th latency bounded, but requires ~15% headroom reserved for probes.

Recommendation: probed-admit as primary admission heuristic, with a soft fixed-slot cap for runaway floods. For the workbook scenario, with 6 pods we meet 95th latency SLO at 1200 tok/s with 18% headroom for probes and 2.2x burst cushion for short spikes.

I also sketched a short runbook for warmup caching: favor predictive prefix caching for known tenants (keeps warmup load local) and limit cross-tenant KV fetches to avoid egress storms. See tab "Admission+Warmup" in the attached.

-Jonas

Diego / Jonas —

Thanks for the model. Procurement notes for the upcoming SOW:
- We need to confirm whether NetGrid's soft reservations are contractually guaranteed (SLA) or an operational best effort. If SLA, add a carveout for cross-tenant KV cache storms.
- Egress shaping: we must document acceptable egress caps and failure modes for customers subject to compliance. Any solution that relies on per-pod software shaping needs an operational playbook for who escalates when caps are hit.
- Pricing: if we require 2.2x burst cushion across 6 pods, that materially affects reserved capacity pricing — we'll likely ask NetGrid for a trial discount/credits for the first 90 days.

Action items:
1) NetGrid: confirm guarantee model for soft reservations and available shaping primitives (hardware vs. software).
2) Diego/Jonas: produce a short appendix with the probe-headroom math and expected token distribution per minute (to be included in the SOW).
3) Laura/Sales: prepare a draft concession ask (credits) for the procurement packet.

Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool — scaling trajectories, admission heuristics, and north-south shaping

Hi Diego / Team,

Appreciate the detail — a few clarifying points from NetGrid side:
1) Soft reservation model: we can offer a two-tier reservation; (a) committed baseline (SLA), and (b) ephemeral burst pool. The burst pool is shared but we can gate it per-tenant with token-bucket policing. We would document failure modes and provide metrics hooks.
2) Egress shaping: we have both hardware TC (at ToR) and software policers at the hypervisor level. HW shaping preserves stronger isolation but requires upfront ToR config and change windows; SW shaping is more flexible.
3) Probe overhead: the 15% probe headroom you mentioned maps well to our telemetry; recommend tagged probe traffic so it’s visible in the dashboard.

We can put together a short tech appendix for the SOW outlining the above and an ops runbook for cap events. Will need a final ask list from you to size committed baseline.

Thanks,
NetGrid Engineering
CloudCo / NetGrid
netgrid-eng@cloudco.com
